Rule_Description: Training resource estimation shall record model parameter count because parameter count directly contributes to model-state memory and is a defining model-size input for training configuration.
Inputs: Model parameter count; training method; precision
Condition: Training resource estimation is being performed
Output_Decision: Record parameter count as an input to training resource estimation
Evidence: Both sources express training model-state memory in terms of parameter count.
Applicability: Training models for which parameter count is known or can be derived from architecture.
Limitations: Parameter count alone does not determine total training memory or compute; activations, optimizer, parallelism and framework overhead also matter.

Rule_Description: Training resource characterization shall record dataset size because the amount of training data affects the number of samples/tokens processed and therefore the training workload.
Inputs: Dataset size; sample count or token count; training epochs/target steps
Output_Decision: Record dataset scale and its representation (samples, tokens, or bytes)
Page_Section_Table: Custom LLaMA training example; data-path/training configuration
Evidence: Megatron training configuration explicitly specifies a data path, training iterations and sequence length; training work is configured over a dataset.
Applicability: Applies to training workloads where dataset size can be represented consistently.
Limitations: Dataset bytes alone do not determine training work; token/sample count, epochs, packing and sampling policy may be more useful.

Rule_Description: Training resource characterization shall record sequence length because training FLOPs and activation behavior depend on sequence length; attention-related work can scale with squared sequence length for dense attention.
Inputs: Sequence length; batch size; model architecture
Output_Decision: Record sequence length for training resource estimation
Exact_Source_Title: Training Examples — Megatron Core; Megatron Bridge FLOP utilities
Evidence: NVIDIA exposes seq-length as a training configuration input and states that attention-core FLOPs use squared sequence-length terms.
Applicability: Transformer/attention workloads and other architectures where sequence length is a material computational dimension.
Limitations: Exact FLOP dependence is architecture-dependent; packed/dynamic sequences require actual sequence statistics rather than one fixed maximum.

Rule_Description: Training characterization shall record both local/micro batch size and global batch size where distributed training is used.
Inputs: Micro-batch size; global batch size; data-parallel size; gradient accumulation
Condition: Training configuration is distributed or batch-controlled
Output_Decision: Record local and global batch-size parameters
Evidence: NVIDIA defines micro-batch size as batch size per model instance and global batch size as training batch size across devices.
Applicability: Applies to Megatron-style distributed training and conceptually to distributed training systems using equivalent definitions.
Limitations: Exact relationship changes with gradient accumulation and data-parallel degree.

Rule_Description: Training characterization shall record the numerical precision used for training because precision affects memory footprint and can affect training throughput.
Inputs: Precision mode; model parameters; gradients; optimizer representation
Unit: FP32 / FP16 / BF16 / FP8 / other supported format
Output_Decision: Record training precision and mixed-precision policy
Evidence: NVIDIA states that reduced precision requires less memory and can accelerate arithmetic-intensive operations; mixed precision retains selected FP32 state.
Applicability: Only where the chosen framework/model/hardware supports the precision mode.
Limitations: Precision does not by itself guarantee a particular speedup or quality outcome; model-specific validation is required.

Rule_Name: Training Compute Demand Depends on Model and Sequence Configuration
Rule_Description: Training compute demand shall be estimated from model/configuration-specific FLOP accounting rather than from parameter count alone.
Inputs: Model architecture; parameter count; batch size; sequence length; actual sequence statistics; training step configuration
Output_Decision: Use a model-specific FLOP estimator or validated benchmark rather than a universal parameter-to-FLOP constant
Evidence: NVIDIA's implementation accepts batch size, sequence-length sums/squared sums and model configuration to calculate FLOPs.
Applicability: Model-specific estimator required.
Limitations: There is no single universal FLOP formula valid for all model architectures; attention, MLP, vision and cross-attention terms differ.

Rule_Name: Required Training Performance Must Meet Target
Rule_Description: A selected training configuration must provide sufficient validated training performance to satisfy the workload's target training-time or time-to-quality requirement.
Inputs: Required training time; target quality; candidate training performance
Condition: Candidate can be evaluated on a comparable workload
Unit: Candidate meets the performance objective; otherwise it fails the training target
Output_Decision: Constraint
Evidence: MLPerf Training measures wall-clock time to train a specified model on a specified dataset to a specified quality target.
Applicability: Only comparable benchmark/workload evidence should be transferred.
Limitations: Do not convert MLPerf results into universal GPU or cluster requirements.

Rule_Description: For training workloads with a defined quality target, wall-clock time to reach that target shall be retained as the primary end-to-end training performance measure.
Inputs: Dataset; model; target quality; elapsed training time
Output_Decision: Store time-to-target-quality for comparable training configurations
Evidence: MLPerf defines benchmark performance as wall-clock time required to reach the specified quality target.
Applicability: Benchmark methodology; actual project target may use another explicit stopping criterion.
Limitations: No universal acceptable time exists across workloads.

Rule_Name: Training Throughput in Samples per Second
Rule_Description: Where training work is measured in samples, throughput may be represented as processed samples divided by elapsed training time.
Inputs: Number of samples processed; elapsed training time
Condition: A sample-based workload metric is available
Output_Decision: Calculate and store sample throughput for the evaluated training configuration
Exact_Source_Title: Derived from MLPerf training timing methodology and standard throughput definition
Evidence: MLPerf provides wall-clock training time; throughput is derived when sample count is known.
Applicability: Derived metric, not a universal MLPerf Training metric for every benchmark.
Limitations: Use only when the numerator is well-defined and comparable between configurations.
Validation_Status: Derived Formula — no supervisor approval required for reporting metric

Rule_Name: Training Throughput in Tokens per Second
Rule_Description: For token-based training workloads, token throughput may be represented as total training tokens processed divided by elapsed training time.
Inputs: Total training tokens; elapsed training time
Output_Decision: Calculate and store token throughput for the evaluated configuration
Evidence: NVIDIA reports tokens/sec/GPU as a training performance metric and tracks token counts in FLOP accounting.
Applicability: Especially applicable to language-model training.
Limitations: Token throughput is workload/configuration-specific and must not be treated as a universal hardware capability.

Rule_Name: Multi-GPU Training Requires Explicit Parallelism Strategy
Rule_Description: When training spans multiple GPUs, the DSS shall record the parallelism strategy rather than treating GPU count alone as the scaling mechanism.
Inputs: GPU count; DP/TP/PP/CP/EP configuration; model architecture
Output_Decision: Record the selected distributed-parallelism strategy before evaluating scale-up performance
Page_Section_Table: Overview; Combining Strategies; Choosing the Right Strategy
Evidence: Megatron Core distinguishes DP, TP, PP, CP and EP and supports combinations of them.
Applicability: Applicable to distributed training frameworks with equivalent strategies.
Limitations: The appropriate strategy depends on model architecture, memory constraints, sequence length and communication behavior.

Rule_Description: In data parallel training, replicas process portions of the batch; therefore global batch size and data-parallel degree must be retained in resource estimation.
Inputs: Global batch size; micro-batch size; data-parallel size; gradient accumulation
Output_Decision: Include data-parallel degree when determining distributed batch configuration
Evidence: NVIDIA states that standard data parallelism replicates the model and splits the batch across GPUs.
Applicability: Applies to standard data parallelism; sharded variants change memory placement.
Limitations: Does not imply linear performance scaling.

Rule_Description: Tensor parallelism shall be considered when individual model layers or their state cannot fit comfortably on one GPU or when the selected training architecture requires layer-wise sharding.
Inputs: Model architecture; per-GPU memory requirement; TP degree
Output_Decision: Represent TP degree explicitly in the training configuration
Evidence: NVIDIA describes TP as splitting individual model layers across GPUs and identifies large layers and GPU memory constraints as use cases.
Applicability: Model/framework-specific.
Limitations: Do not infer a universal TP threshold from the examples in NVIDIA documentation.

Rule_Description: Pipeline parallelism shall be represented explicitly when model layers are distributed across pipeline stages.
Inputs: Number of layers; PP degree; pipeline schedule
Output_Decision: Represent PP degree and pipeline configuration in the training resource model
Evidence: NVIDIA describes PP as splitting model layers vertically by depth across GPUs.
Applicability: Model/framework-specific.
Limitations: Pipeline bubbles and stage imbalance affect realized performance; no universal efficiency value should be assumed.

Rule_Name: Total GPU Count From Parallelism Degrees
Rule_Description: For a Megatron-style configuration combining the documented parallelism axes, total GPU count is the product of the configured parallelism degrees.
Inputs: TP; PP; CP; EP; DP
Output_Decision: Compute the configured training world size from parallelism degrees
Evidence: NVIDIA explicitly states Total GPUs = TP × PP × CP × EP × DP.
Applicability: Specific to the documented Megatron Core parallelism model.
Limitations: Do not use this to claim that the resulting GPU count is optimal or sufficient for a workload.

Rule_Name: Do Not Assume Linear Multi-GPU Training Scaling
Rule_Description: The DSS shall not assume that doubling GPU count halves training time; scaling efficiency must be measured or validated for the workload and configuration.
Inputs: Single-GPU or baseline time; multi-GPU time; GPU counts; configuration
Output_Decision: Use measured/validated scaling efficiency for training-time projection
Evidence: MLCommons reports multi-node scaling results and notes that scaling behavior varies with communication and utilization; it does not establish ideal linear scaling.
Applicability: General engineering constraint; exact efficiency is workload/system dependent.
Limitations: Never convert a particular benchmark scaling result into a universal efficiency threshold.

Rule_Name: Training Memory Includes Model State Components
Rule_Description: Training memory estimation shall account for parameters, gradients and optimizer state, with master weights included where the selected mixed-precision optimizer representation requires them.
Inputs: Parameter count; parameter precision; gradient precision; optimizer state; master-weight representation
Output_Decision: Produce model-state memory components before adding activation/runtime overhead
Evidence: Sources explicitly decompose model-state memory into weights, gradients and optimizer-related state; 10Cache includes FP32 master parameters in its mixed-precision Adam/AdamW example.
Applicability: Only for the optimizer/precision assumptions represented by the source formula.
Limitations: Existing WLR-F-02 and WLR-F-04 are already present and should remain; this rule clarifies their component scope rather than replacing them.

Rule_Name: Activation Memory Is Separate From Model-State Memory
Rule_Description: Training resource estimation shall treat activation memory as a separate component from parameter/gradient/optimizer-state memory.
Inputs: Sequence length; batch size; model architecture; activation-checkpointing policy
Output_Decision: Add or estimate activation memory separately from model-state memory
Evidence: NVIDIA states that activation memory footprint grows about linearly with sequence length and discusses activation recomputation as a memory/performance tradeoff.
Applicability: Architecture-dependent and especially relevant to transformer training.
Limitations: No universal closed-form activation-memory formula is supported by this source; do not invent one.
Validation_Status: Verified concept; quantitative formula remains gap

Rule_Name: Communication Buffers Are Distinct Training Memory
Rule_Description: Where distributed training uses collective communication, communication buffers shall be considered separately when estimating peak training memory if the framework exposes them.
Inputs: Parallelism strategy; collective communication; buffer configuration
Output_Decision: Include framework-exposed communication-buffer memory where material
Evidence: Megatron documents parameter gathering/reduction overlap and distributed optimizer communication, showing communication is part of distributed training execution.
Applicability: Framework-specific.
Limitations: No universal communication-buffer size formula is established by the source; keep as a measured/configuration input.
Validation_Status: Verified concept; quantitative formula remains gap

Rule_Name: Training Duration Must Be Explicitly Defined
Rule_Description: Training resource planning shall distinguish elapsed training duration from target time-to-train and from time-to-target-quality.
Inputs: Training duration; target quality; target training time
Condition: Training plan includes a time objective
Output_Decision: Record the applicable duration objective and stopping criterion
Evidence: Scenarios & Metrics
Confidence: MLPerf uses elapsed wall-clock time to a quality target, demonstrating that a training objective must be tied to a defined stopping criterion.
Applicability: High
Limitations: Applies to quality-targeted training; fixed-step or fixed-epoch workloads need their own stopping definition.
Validation_Status: Do not infer a universal training duration from model size alone.
